mainEntity.name: How much does a Volkswagen Polo 1.5 TSI engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Volkswagen Polo 1.5 TSI engine replacement typically costs £1,800-£3,800 for a reconditioned or rebuilt unit supply-only, with fitting adding £700-£1,200 depending on the workshop. Used engines: £1,200-£2,000 depending on code and mileage. Reconditioned: £1,800-£3,000. Rebuilt: £2,200-£3,800. Full supply & fit: £2,500-£5,000 total.

mainEntity.name: What is the most common failure on the Volkswagen Polo 1.5 TSI engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most frequently reported issues are injector clogging causing cold-start problems, rough idle and misfires, low-speed drivability issues ('kangaroo effect') on early DADA/DPCA engines, water pump failure (plastic impeller detachment), and timing belt replacement at the extended 140,000-mile interval. Oil consumption can also be higher during early life.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Volkswagen Polo 1.5 TSI?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's value and condition. A typical Polo 1.5 TSI (2018-2022) is worth £8,000-£18,000. If the car is worth under £8,000 and needs a full engine replacement, carefully evaluate against scrap value. If the car is worth £10,000+, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine (£1,800-£3,800) is usually financially viable. If injectors have failed but the engine block is intact, injector cleaning or replacement (£150-£800) is often the most cost-effective solution.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Volkswagen Polo 1.5 TSI engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical Volkswagen Polo 1.5 TSI engine replacement takes 1-3 days for a specialist workshop. Timing belt replacement: 6-10 hours labour. Injector replacement: 3-5 hours labour. Water pump replacement: 4-6 hours labour. Full engine swap: 10-16 hours depending on engine code and vehicle age. Supply & fit lead time: 3-7 working days from quote acceptance to completion.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between DADA, DPCA and DFYA in the Polo 1.5 TSI?

acceptedAnswer.text: These are different variants of the same EA211 1.5 TSI engine family. DADA / DPCA: 150 hp - found in early Polo Mk6 (2018-2020); some low-speed drivability issues reported. DFYA / DHFA: 150 hp - found in later Polo Mk6 (2019-2022); improved software and emissions calibration. DXDB / DACA: 150 hp - found in current Polo models (2020-present); latest software and emissions updates. All share the same EA211 architecture with Active Cylinder Management (ACT). Enter your registration above to confirm which code is fitted to your Polo.

mainEntity.name: Does a replacement Volkswagen Polo 1.5 TSI engine come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - every rebuilt and reconditioned Volkswagen Polo 1.5 TSI engine supplied through EnginesMarket carries a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Warranty covers manufacturing defects and component failure. Timing belt, water pump and tensioner are replaced with genuine or OEM-quality parts. Injectors are tested and cleaned or replaced as part of the rebuild process. Always confirm exact warranty terms with your chosen supplier before purchase.

historyTimeline.h2: Volkswagen Polo 1.5 TSI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Volkswagen Polo 1.5 TSI, powered by the EA211 engine family, was introduced in the Polo Mk6 (AW/BZ chassis) in 2018 as a replacement for the 1.4 TSI. This 1.5-litre turbocharged petrol engine features Active Cylinder Management (ACT) technology, which deactivates two cylinders under light loads to improve fuel efficiency. Based on the proven EA211 modular engine platform, the 1.5 TSI delivers 150 hp and 250 Nm of torque, combining responsive performance with impressive economy - up to 10% more efficient than its predecessor.

milestones.description: Polo Mk6 (AW1/BZ1) launched with 1.5 TSI engine, 150 hp, engine codes DADA and DPCA
2020 - Early 1.5 TSI engines affected by low-speed drivability issues ("kangaroo effect") and software-related hesitation
DFYA and DHFA engine codes introduced across the Volkswagen Group range
DXDB and DACA variants added; Active Cylinder Management (ACT) standard across all 1.5 TSI units
present - 1.5 TSI continues as a popular powertrain choice for the Polo range

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Volkswagen Polo 1.5 TSI is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Volkswagen Polo 1.5 TSI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Volkswagen Polo 1.5 TSI is a refined and efficient engine, but several well-documented issues can lead to significant repair bills. The EA211 family is generally reliable - with proper maintenance, these engines can achieve 250,000-300,000 km - but early DADA/DPCA codes and injector-related problems have generated replacement demand. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.affectedModels: Volkswagen Polo 1.5 TSI (early DADA/DPCA engines, 2018-2020, manual transmission)
problems.rootCause: Early 1.5 TSI engines suffered from hesitation and jerking during pull-away and low-speed driving, particularly between 1,200-2,000 rpm. The issue is most pronounced in vehicles with manual gearboxes. Volkswagen has acknowledged the problem and released software updates to address it.

repairOptions.longevity: First-line fix; may resolve hesitation issues
If software update doesn't resolve the issue

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Rebuilt engine with updated ECU software
repairOptions.longevity: If drivability issues are accompanied by mechanical failure

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Volkswagen Polo 1.5 TSI (2018-2022) sits in the £8,000-£18,000 range depending on mileage, trim and condition. A software update (£80-£150) is a minor expense. Full engine replacement should only be considered if mechanical failure has occurred.
problems.recommendation: If your Polo 1.5 TSI exhibits hesitation or jerking at low speeds, contact a Volkswagen dealer or specialist to check if your vehicle has the latest ECU software. Many early cars were updated under goodwill or recall programmes. If the issue persists after a software update, a professional diagnostic is recommended.

problems.h4: Fuel Injector Problems - Cold-Start Roughness and Misfires
problems.rootCause: Fuel injectors can become clogged with carbon deposits, leading to inconsistent fuel spray patterns, incomplete combustion, and misfires. Symptoms include rough idle, cold-start problems, stuttering during the first minutes of operation, jerking during acceleration, and increased fuel consumption. In severe cases, injectors may need replacement rather than cleaning.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Professional cleaning of all fuel injectors

repairOptions.longevity: If cleaning fails or injectors are beyond repair

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Rebuilt engine with new injectors and updated components
repairOptions.longevity: If injector failure has caused engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For Polo 1.5 TSI examples under £8,000, injector cleaning (£150-£300) is almost always the right first step. Full injector replacement at £350-£800 should be evaluated against the vehicle's overall condition.
problems.recommendation: Use premium quality fuel and consider a fuel system cleaner periodically to prevent injector clogging. If you experience rough idle, cold-start problems or increased fuel consumption, have the injectors inspected and cleaned professionally. Replacing injectors early prevents more serious engine damage.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt DPCA Volkswagen Polo 1.5 TSI engine prices

problems.affectedModels: Volkswagen Polo 1.5 TSI (all codes, higher-mileage examples)
problems.rootCause: The Polo's water pump features a plastic impeller that can detach from the shaft, causing the pump to spin without circulating coolant. This leads to overheating and potential engine damage. The water pump is located on the opposite side of the engine from the timing belt, meaning it does not need to be replaced with the timing belt as on some other engines.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New water pump with metal impeller upgrade
repairOptions.longevity: If pump has failed or is leaking

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full coolant flush and system inspection
repairOptions.longevity: Preventative maintenance; recommended with pump replacement
If overheating persists after pump replacement

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Water pump replacement (£250-£500) is a routine maintenance expense on any Polo 1.5 TSI. This repair is almost always worth doing regardless of vehicle value.
problems.recommendation: Watch for signs of water pump failure: coolant leaks, engine temperature warning light, or the engine temperature running higher than normal. If you notice any of these symptoms, have the cooling system inspected immediately. When replacing the water pump, consider upgrading to a unit with a metal impeller for improved longevity.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt DFYA Volkswagen Polo 1.5 TSI engine prices

problems.h4: Timing Belt Service - The EA211's Critical Maintenance Item
problems.affectedModels: Volkswagen Polo 1.5 TSI (all codes) Typical service interval: 140,000 miles / 15 years (no time limit)
problems.rootCause: The EA211 family uses a dry timing belt (not a chain). Unlike older TSI engines with problematic timing chains, the 1.5 TSI's belt is durable but requires specialist tools for accurate timing replacement. If the belt fails, valve and piston damage is likely.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full belt kit with tensioner, idler and water pump (if belt-driven)
Head removal, valve replacement and refitting
repairOptions.longevity: If belt has snapped but bottom end is intact

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Rebuilt engine with new timing belt and components
repairOptions.longevity: If belt failure has caused bottom-end damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For Polo 1.5 TSI examples worth £8,000+, timing belt replacement (£500-£900) is a routine maintenance expense. For vehicles approaching 140,000 miles, this is essential preventative maintenance.
problems.recommendation: The 1.5 TSI's timing belt has an extended service interval of 140,000 miles, but always follow the manufacturer's recommendations and use a specialist with the correct timing tools. If you hear unusual noises from the belt area or notice oil leaks from the camshaft adjuster retainers, have the system inspected immediately.
